decisions.reason: Bleaching tray blanks remain a good fit with the firm's dental laboratory materials portfolio, and their earlier multi-model launch with dedicated web support suggests they are still worth maintaining unless demand proves too small.

The PETG thermoforming blank sits very close to the firm's established dental materials and workflow business, so a large quality-focused manufacturer would normally continue it rather than free only limited resources by dropping it.

The UV-curing lacquer is more exposed because it had weaker visibility and is a more auxiliary material, but it still complements the firm's custom-device workflow and is not yet peripheral enough to justify withdrawal.

Intraoral contrast spray supports digital scanning workflows that match the firm's strategic direction, though evolving scanner technology makes it somewhat more vulnerable than the core thermoforming products.
The custom earmold line fits the firm's hearing-care capabilities and custom manufacturing strengths well, so despite modest web prominence it remains strategically coherent to keep on the market.
